source_text: [1] Μὴ οὖν ἀναισθητῶμεν τῆς χρηστότητος αὐτοῦ. ἐὰν γὰρ ἡμᾶς μιμήσηται καθὰ πράσσομεν, οὐκέτι ἐσμέν. διὰ τοῦτο, μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ γενόμενοι, μάθωμεν κατὰ Χριστιανισμὸν ζῆν. ὃς γὰρ ἄλλῳ ὀνόματι καλεῖται πλέον τούτου, οὐκ ἔστιν τοῦ θεοῦ. [2] ὑπέρθεσθε οὖν τὴν κακὴν ζύμην, τὴν παλαιωθεῖσαν καὶ ἐνοξίσασαν, καὶ μεταβάλεσθε εἰς νέαν ζύμην, ὅ ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός. ἁλίσθητε ἐν αὐτῷ, ἵνα μὴ διαφθαρῇ τις ἐν ὑμῖν, ἐπεὶ ἀπὸ τῆς ὀσμῆς ἐλεγχθήσεσθε. [3] ἄτοπόν ἐστιν, Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν λαλεῖν καὶ ἰουδαΐζειν. ὁ γὰρ Χριστιανισμὸς οὐκ εἰς Ἰουδαῖσμὸν ἐπίστευσεν, ἀλλ’ Ἰουδαϊσμὸς εἰς Χριστιανισμόν, ᾧ πᾶσα γλῶσσα πιστεύσασα εἰς θεὸν συνήχθη.
pass_a_gloss: Let us not, then, be insensible to his kindness. For if he were to imitate us in the way we act, we would no longer exist. Therefore, having become his disciples, let us learn to live according to Christianity. For whoever is called by another name besides this is not of God. Put aside, then, the bad leaven, which has grown old and sour, and be changed into the new leaven, which is Jesus Christ. Be salted in him, so that no one among you goes bad, since you will be convicted by your smell. It is absurd to speak of Jesus Christ and to practice Judaism. For Christianity did not believe into Judaism, but Judaism into Christianity, into which every tongue that believed in God was gathered together.

lemmas.gloss: live as a Jew, practice Judaism

pass_b_english: So let us not be numb to his kindness. If he were to imitate the way we behave, we would cease to exist. Since we have become his disciples, then, let us learn to live by Christianity. Whoever goes by any other name than this does not belong to God.

Get rid of the bad leaven, gone stale and sour, and be changed into the new leaven, which is Jesus Christ (1 Corinthians 5:7–8). Be salted in him, so that none of you rots, for by your smell you will be found out.

It is absurd to talk of Jesus Christ and practice Judaism. Christianity did not put its faith in Judaism; Judaism put its faith in Christianity, where every tongue that believes in God has been gathered.

choices.term: ἐὰν γὰρ ἡμᾶς μιμήσηται καθὰ πράσσομεν
choices.english: If he were to imitate the way we behave
choices.why: The verb is 'imitate': if God acted as we act, we would perish. 'Reward' is a paraphrase.
rejected: were He to reward us according to our works

choices.english: by your smell you will be found out
choices.why: Continues the leaven and salt image: rot gives itself away.
rejected: by your savour you shall be convicted

choices.term: ὁ Χριστιανισμὸς οὐκ εἰς Ἰουδαϊσμὸν ἐπίστευσεν
choices.english: Christianity did not put its faith in Judaism
choices.why: πιστεύω εἰς kept as believing into; his chiasm kept.
Living by Jewish custom; neutral modern wording.

anf_compare.notes: ANF 'were He to reward us according to our works' paraphrases μιμήσηται (imitate). ANF 'gathered together to God' misreads the relative ᾧ: every tongue was gathered into Christianity, having believed in God. Rest same sense.

notes: 'Every tongue' may echo Philippians 2:11 or Isaiah 45:23; 'salted' may recall Mark 9:49-50; 'another name' may recall Acts 4:12 or 11:26. None cited inline.

checker_dispute: checker b called the inline (1 Corinthians 5:7–8) a false addition. The Greek 'ὑπέρθεσθε οὖν τὴν κακὴν ζύμην, τὴν παλαιωθεῖσαν ... μεταβάλεσθε εἰς νέαν ζύμην' takes up Paul's old/new leaven ('ἐκκαθάρατε τὴν παλαιὰν ζύμην, ἵνα ἦτε νέον φύραμα'), and house rule (TRANSLATION_QA.md) requires every clear allusion to be cited inline in Pass B. Kept.

review.notes: p1 checked clause by clause. 'Μὴ οὖν ἀναισθητῶμεν τῆς χρηστότητος αὐτοῦ' matches A 'Let us not, then, be insensible to his kindness' and B 'So let us not be numb to his kindness'. 'ἐὰν γὰρ ἡμᾶς μιμήσηται καθὰ πράσσομεν, οὐκέτι ἐσμέν' keeps his imitating us and nonexistence in A 'imitate us in the way we act, we would no longer exist' and B 'imitate the way we behave, we would cease to exist'. Negations hold: 'οὐκ ἔστιν τοῦ θεοῦ' and 'οὐκ εἰς Ἰουδαῖσμὸν ἐπίστευσεν, ἀλλ’ Ἰουδαϊσμὸς εἰς Χριστιανισμόν' are not reversed in A or B. 'ὅ ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός', the salt purpose 'ἵνα μὴ διαφθαρῇ τις ἐν ὑμῖν', and 'ἀπὸ τῆς ὀσμῆς ἐλεγχθήσεσθε' remain. B's '(1 Corinthians 5:7–8)' is a required inline identification beside the old/new leaven clause, not an added claim. Title 'The New Leaven' names the thought. No OCR damage in the locked text.
